title: Wire thread_panel integration
description: Modify lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua to integrate reply_input, thread_menu, and observer. Changes: (1) Add requires for data, observers, orchestration, reply_input, thread_menu. (2) Subscribe to 'comments' observer in show(), unsubscribe in close() — enables optimistic update reflection. (3) Add submit_reply() local fn: get text, clear input, call orchestration.submit_reply, restore text on failure. (4) Add toggle_resolved() local fn: call orchestration.toggle_resolved. (5) Add open_menu() local fn: call thread_menu.open with callbacks. (6) Map <C-s> and <C-a> on panel buffer, map <C-s>/<C-a>/q/? on input buffer. (7) In update(): clear reply input when thread ID changes. (8) In close(): unsubscribe → close menu → close reply_input → unmount panel. (9) Update hint_registry with C-s/Submit and C-a/Actions. TDD: extend tests/display/thread_panel_spec.lua first.

title: Create reply_input module with TDD
description: Create lua/nit/display/reply_input.lua — manages editable input window below thread panel. Uses nvim_open_win with split='below' targeting panel window. Public API: open(panel_winid), close(), is_open(), get_text(), set_text(text), clear(), get_bufnr(), get_winid(), map(mode, lhs, rhs, opts). Buffer: scratch, markdown, modifiable. Window: winfixheight, no numbers/signs, NormalFloat background, height 5. Winbar shows C-s Submit hint using NitThreadHintKey/NitThreadHintLabel. TDD: write tests/display/reply_input_spec.lua first (closed-state guards, text get/set/clear), then implement.

title: Bug: resolved threads excluded from thread panel
description: manager.lua filter_displayable has 'and not thread.isResolved' condition that prevents resolved threads from being displayed in the thread panel. Resolved threads should be viewable — the user explicitly opened that thread. Fix: remove the isResolved exclusion from filter_displayable in lua/nit/display/manager.lua.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree: isResolved condition removed from filter_displayable in manager.lua

title: Right-align viewer comment headers in thread panel
description:
Thread panel comment headers (@author · time) are all left-aligned. To create a chat-like visual distinction, the current GitHub user's headers should be right-aligned while other users' stay left-aligned. Body text stays left-aligned for all comments.

Requires: fetching viewer's GitHub login, storing in state, and using it to conditionally pad header lines in format_thread.

Success criteria:
- get_viewer_login/set_viewer_login/clear work in state/data.lua
- api/viewer.lua fetches login via gh api user
- controller.lua wires viewer fetch into startup (parallel with fetch_pr)
- format_thread right-aligns headers for viewer's own comments
- get_line_highlights returns text_col for correct extmark column offset
- Optimistic comment author uses real viewer login

Anti-patterns:
- Do NOT hardcode viewer login
- Do NOT block PR load on viewer fetch (must be parallel/independent)
- Do NOT skip graceful degradation when viewer login is nil
close_reason: all 6 steps implemented; 465 tests pass; lint and typecheck clean

2. Wire fetch_viewer into controller.lua (GREEN)

## Success criteria
- [ ] load fetches viewer login alongside fetch_pr
- [ ] viewer login stored via data.set_viewer_login on success
- [ ] viewer failure silently degrades (no error set)
- [ ] cleanup cancels in-flight viewer fetch
close_reason: fetch_viewer wired into controller; cancel_viewer tracked; 3 new tests pass (2 truly new + 1 already passing)

title: Add zebra-stripe backgrounds to thread panel comments
description: Comments in the thread panel blend together. Add alternating background colors to provide visual separation between comments. Even-indexed comments get a subtle tinted background (NitThreadCommentAlt) via extmarks with hl_eol=true, which handles window resize automatically. Odd comments keep the default background.

title: Bug: keybinding hints scroll with panel content
description: The keybinding hints in the thread panel are rendered as part of the scrollable buffer, so they scroll out of view when the thread is long. Hints should be pinned to the window bottom. Fix: render hints in a separate non-scrollable region (e.g., statusline, winbar, or a pinned extmark at a fixed position) in lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua.
close_reason: Fixed: hints moved from scrollable buffer to winbar; superseded by new help popup feature

title: Ctrl+w q closes thread panel and reply input separately instead of whole sidebar
description:
When the thread panel is open with a reply input below it, pressing Ctrl+w q (window close) closes only the focused window (panel or input) rather than the entire sidebar as a unit.

Expected: Ctrl+w q on any window in the sidebar (thread panel or reply input) closes the whole sidebar — equivalent to pressing q or Esc.

Actual: Ctrl+w q closes only the currently focused window, leaving the other window orphaned.

title: Explore virtual text usage for comment previews
description: Investigate how virtual text (extmarks) can surface review comment previews directly in source buffers. Currently the only visual indicators are gutter signs and subtle line-range highlights. Virtual text could show a compact comment summary (author + first line) without opening the thread panel. Key considerations: behavior in narrow diff splits (codediff.nvim), end-of-line vs virtual lines, truncation strategy, and avoiding disruption of diff line alignment.

title: Apply alternating backgrounds in thread panel update()
description: Extend the extmark loop in lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua update() to track a comment_index counter. For even-indexed comments, apply line_hl_group=NitThreadCommentAlt with hl_eol=true to every line (author + body + trailing blank). For author lines in even comments, use NitThreadCommentAlt instead of CursorLine. Odd comments keep existing styling.

title: Phase 15: command wiring
description: Public Lua API and :Nit subcommands connecting all v1.1 features. Success criteria: (1) require('nit').menu() opens context-aware action menu; (2) require('nit').next_comment() and prev_comment() navigate between comments; (3) :Nit menu, :Nit next, :Nit prev subcommands work and appear in completion; (4) plugin registers no automatic keybindings. Requirements: API-01, API-02, API-03, API-04, API-05. Depends on Phase 8 (navigation, already done), Phase 12, Phase 14.

title: Phase 12: thread popup interaction
description: Add reply input, submit, and resolve toggle to the thread popup. Success criteria: (1) user can type a reply in an input area and submit with C-s, which sends to GitHub immediately; (2) user can toggle resolved state with C-r from within the popup; (3) popup updates immediately after submit (optimistic update end-to-end); (4) on mutation failure, popup reverts to previous state and user sees error notification. Requirements: THRD-03, THRD-04, THRD-05. Depends on Phase 10 (orchestrated mutations) and Phase 11 bugs being fixed.

title: Create thread_menu module with TDD
description: Create lua/nit/display/thread_menu.lua — context-aware action menu for thread panel. Uses nui.popup (same pattern as help_popup.lua). Public API: open(thread, callbacks), close(), is_open(). Callbacks table: { on_toggle_resolved: fun() }. Menu content is context-aware: shows 'r Resolve thread' when unresolved, 'r Unresolve thread' when resolved. Keybindings: r executes action + closes, q/Esc closes without action. TDD: write tests/display/thread_menu_spec.lua first, then implement.

title: Add NitThreadCommentAlt highlight group
description: Add a computed highlight group NitThreadCommentAlt to lua/nit/ui/highlights.lua. Use existing blend() to mix accent color into NormalFloat bg at ~10% alpha. Fallback: link to CursorLine if colors can't be resolved.

title: Bug: text wrapping in thread panel is hard to read
description: Thread panel needs breakindent=true and list=false in win_options for readable long-line wrapping. Currently long comment lines wrap without indentation, making wrapped text hard to distinguish from new paragraphs. Fix: add breakindent=true, list=false to the window options in lua/nit/display/thread_panel.lua Split creation.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree: breakindent=true and list=false added to thread panel win_options

title: Thread menu: right-align hotkeys and support direct keybindings
description:
Two changes to the thread action menu:

1. Right-align hotkey hints in menu items (e.g. 'Resolve thread' left-aligned, 'r' right-aligned with padding to fill menu width).

2. Menu item hotkeys should work as direct keybindings on the thread panel — pressing 'r' in the panel (menu closed) should resolve/unresolve the thread directly, same as opening the menu and pressing 'r'. This makes the menu a discoverable reference for shortcuts that already work.

title: Equalize window layout after thread panel mount/close
description: When the thread panel opens via vertical botright 60split, it takes 60 chars from the adjacent window rather than distributing the cost across all windows. Running wincmd = (Ctrl+w =) after mount fixes multi-window layouts (e.g., codediff.nvim) but naively equalizing makes the thread panel too wide in simple layouts (single file + panel). Need an intelligent approach: equalize non-nit windows while preserving the thread panel's fixed width. Consider: run wincmd = then re-set panel width, or selectively resize only the diff windows.

title: Phase 14: context menu
description: Floating context-aware action menu driven by cursor position and thread state. Success criteria: (1) user can open menu via command or Lua API from any buffer with PR context; (2) when cursor is on a commented line, menu includes 'Open thread'; when not, that action is absent (not greyed out); (3) each menu item displays its hotkey right-aligned; (4) selecting action executes it and closes menu. Requirements: MENU-01, MENU-02, MENU-03, MENU-04. Depends on Phase 12.

title: Phase 13: mutation queue
description: Rate-limited queue for mutations to avoid GitHub's secondary rate limit. Success criteria: (1) rapid consecutive mutations are queued and spaced with minimum 1100ms delay; (2) on mutation failure, user sees actionable error notification via vim.notify; (3) queue testable end-to-end through thread popup. Requirements: MUT-04, MUT-05. Depends on Phase 12.

title: Add ? help popup to thread panel
description: Replace inline winbar hints with a ? keybinding that opens a floating help popup showing all registered hints. Winbar shows only thread title. Popup reads from hint_registry, uses nui.Popup pattern from comment_popup.lua, closes on q/Esc/?.
close_reason: Implemented help_popup.lua module, wired ? keybinding in thread_panel, winbar now shows title + ? Help indicator only

title: Action menu: Enter should trigger item under cursor
description: When the thread action menu is opened via <C-a>, pressing Enter does nothing. It should execute the action on the line under the cursor. Currently, menu items are only triggerable via their shortcut key (e.g. 'r' for resolve). Adding <CR> support makes the menu behave like a standard selection list.
